text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes where standard upscalers blur edges or lose texture—critical for high-contrast power lines, rusted metal, or foliage. The trade-off is a 15% slower render time, but the 0.8% quality bump justifies it for final outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting cycles on a dead-end fix while high-motion scenes still ghost. Test VFI-Flow’s temporal super-resolution instead; if it handles motion blur without ghosting, that’s the 0.5%+ gain we need.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly attacking the ghosting problem Torque flagged—no other tool converts temporal blur to clean detail. The trade-off is a 20% longer per-frame render, but the 1.1% quality jump on fast-moving power lines and rusted metal outweighs it; depth-aware upscaling can’t touch motion artifacts, so this is the only move that actually raises EXCAVA’s capability.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s temporal super-resolution will still ghost on high-motion scenes—its artifact is baked into the model, not the input. Test it on EXCAVA’s worst-case motion samples first; if it fails, fall back to a hybrid: use InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler for spatial detail *and* add a motion-compensated frame interpolation step (like RIFE) to clean temporal artifacts—then measure the net gain.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Hybrid pipeline—run VFI-Flow only on keyframes with worst motion blur, then apply InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to all frames. Result: 1.3% quality gain on high-motion scenes with minimal render overhead. Owner: Gearbox.
